experiment: Hypothesis re-test on more protein-ligand datasets/splits (RSNN_TRSF vs GET)
hypothesis: A param-matched plain transformer (dropout0.1, all-atom + 4.5A distance graph, 692k params) reaches statistical parity with the equivariant GET, and chemistry-informed tweaks don't help. Established on PDBbind-Benchmark identity30 (RSNN 0.5847 vs GET 0.5887). Now re-tested on other splits + a new dataset.
config_under_test: dropout0.1 = --base transformer --h_dim 120 --num_layers 3 --nhead 4 --ffn_mult 4 --pos_enc rope --attn_mode full --reduce mean --dropout 0.1 --m 6 --w 8 --max_len 448 --ligand_max_len 72 --angles 1 --dihedrals 1 (~692k params). 3 seeds. Plus grid points causal (rope/causal/dropout0) + lr5e4 (lr 5e-4) at seed42.

identity60.verdict: RSNN BEATS GET on identity60: Pearson 0.6855 vs 0.6685 (non-overlapping bands), also better RMSE + MAE. causal/lr5e4 pending.

scaffold.verdict: PARITY (RSNN nominally ahead, overlapping bands): RSNN 0.4771 vs GET 0.4615; RSNN also slightly better RMSE (1.555 vs 1.5627) + MAE (1.2311 vs 1.2471). Grid points ~comparable.

lba.verdict: GET modestly beats RSNN on LBA: 0.6165 vs 0.5946 (barely non-overlapping), also better RMSE/MAE. Grid points inferior (causal 0.5718, lr5e4 0.5286 < 0.5946).

results.note: GET Pearson varies sharply by split difficulty: scaffold 0.4615 (hard) < identity30 0.5887 < identity60 0.6685 (easy). The RSNN-vs-GET comparison is per-split (each config trains its own; label/split distributions differ).

verdict: REPLICATES. Across 3 PDBbind splits + Atom3D LBA, the param-matched plain transformer (RSNN_TRSF dropout0.1, 692k) is COMPETITIVE with the equivariant GET -- differences <=0.022 Pearson, mostly within overlapping error bars, neither systematically ahead. RSNN nominally wins 2/4 (identity60 clearly non-overlapping +0.017; scaffold +0.016 overlapping), GET wins 2/4 (LBA +0.022 modest; identity30 +0.004 marginal/overlapping). On RMSE/MAE the same trade: RSNN better on id60+scaffold, GET better on id30+LBA. Conclusion: 'plain param-matched transformer roughly matches equivariant GET' holds robustly on protein-ligand affinity; and no chemistry/config lever helped (causal/lr5e4 here; earlier param-bump, ligand bond-graph, protein torsion-order all hurt or tied). GET's absolute score swings with split difficulty (scaffold 0.46 < id30 0.59 < LBA 0.62 < id60 0.67); comparison is within-split.
